name: Customer support email triage: classify, log and draft AI replies in Gmail

parameters.content:
## Customer support email triage: classify, log and draft AI replies in Gmail

### How it works

Every support email that lands in your Gmail inbox is read by AI and sorted into one of four categories: product question, billing issue, urgent complaint, or spam/notification. Real requests are logged as a ticket row in Google Sheets, and the AI writes a reply grounded in your own FAQ — saved as a **draft in the original thread**, never sent automatically, so a human always presses Send.

Urgent complaints additionally ping your team in Slack the moment they arrive, so an angry customer never waits until someone checks the inbox. Spam and automated notifications are filtered out before they waste anyone's attention.

The FAQ lives in a plain text field inside the workflow — no knowledge base, vector store or extra service to set up. Paste your policies once and the drafts speak with your voice.

### Setup steps

Takes ≈10 minutes.

- Connect your Gmail account in **When Support Email Arrives** and **Send Draft Via Gmail** (one click on n8n Cloud).
- Open **Set FAQ and Policies** and replace the placeholder text with your actual FAQ, refund policy, business hours and anything else replies should be based on.
- Connect an OpenAI (or compatible) credential in **OpenAI Support Model**.
- Create a spreadsheet with columns `Date, From, Subject, Category` and select it in **Log Ticket in Sheets**.
- Optional: paste a Slack incoming-webhook URL into **Post Alert to Slack** (api.slack.com/apps → Incoming Webhooks). Delete the node if you don't use Slack.
- Activate the workflow. It polls your inbox every minute.

### Customization

- **Categories:** edit them directly in **Classify Request with AI** — add "feature request" or "partnership", give each a one-line description, and wire the new output to whichever action you like.
- **Tone of the drafts:** edit the system message in **Generate AI Reply Draft**. Add your sign-off, languages, or a "keep it under 100 words" rule.
- **Send instead of draft:** in **Send Draft Via Gmail** switch the resource from Draft to Message — only recommended once you trust the FAQ coverage.
- **Different helpdesk:** the same pattern works with any IMAP trigger, or swap the Sheets log for Airtable/Notion.
- **Escalation channel:** replace the Slack webhook with a Discord webhook or a Telegram bot call — it's a plain HTTP request.

## Watch the support inbox

Polls Gmail every minute. The FAQ node holds the knowledge every AI draft is written from — edit it once, all replies follow.

## Classify each email with AI

Reads the sender, subject and preview and sorts the email into question, billing, urgent complaint, or spam. Add or rename categories to fit your business.

## Route by category

Real requests are tagged and move on to logging and drafting. Urgent complaints also ping the team in Slack immediately. Spam stops here.

## Log the ticket and draft the reply

Appends a ticket row to Google Sheets, has AI write a reply grounded in your FAQ, and saves it as a Gmail draft in the original thread. A human always presses Send.

assignments.value:
CHANGE ME — paste your real FAQ and policies here. For example:

Q: How do I reset my password?
A: Click 'Forgot password' on the login page. The reset link is valid for 24 hours.

Q: What is your refund policy?
A: Full refund within 14 days of purchase, no questions asked. Email us your order number.

Q: What are your support hours?
A: Monday-Friday, 9:00-17:00 CET. We answer within one business day.

Company voice: friendly, concise, first-person plural ('we'). Sign every reply as 'The Support Team'.

categories.description: A customer asks how to do something, how the product works, or anything answerable from documentation
Payments, refunds, invoices, subscriptions, pricing or account charges
An angry or frustrated customer, something is broken or blocking them, threat to cancel
Newsletters, automated notifications, receipts, cold outreach — anything that is not a real support request

=You are a customer support agent. Write a complete, ready-to-send reply email.

Rules:
- Base every factual statement ONLY on the FAQ below. If the FAQ does not cover the question, write a short, polite holding reply saying the team will follow up — never invent an answer.
- For billing issues, ask for the order number if it is not in the message.
- For urgent complaints, open with a sincere apology and make clear a human is on it.
- Output only the email body, no subject line.
